title: The Teensy Executable Revisited
summary: This article revisits techniques for creating extremely small executable programs, continuing the author's famous work on minimal ELF binaries (including the legendary 45-byte 'teny' program). It explores advanced low-level programming tricks to minimize executable size while maintaining functionality.
problem_solved: It explores the challenge of creating the smallest possible working executable programs by understanding and exploiting ELF binary format specifications and operating system requirements.
why_valuable: Pushing executable size to the limit reveals deep insights into how operating systems load and execute programs, teaching fundamental concepts about ELF structure, system calls, and binary format specifications.
